To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) noise injection is an important data augmentation technique, (b) the noise magnitude is a key parameter for noise injection, (c) the noise model is not as important as the magnitude, (d) SSIM is a useful metric in determining the noise magnitudes, and (e) the noise injection is not a substitute for other data augmentation techniques.
• The optimal noise level is the one that maximizes the SSIM value between noisy and noise-free versions of an image.

(1) The best noise model to use for CNNs is Gaussian noise with a mean of 0.0 and a standard deviation of 0.1, (2) Noise injection should be done in the training data, not in the validation and test data, and (3) Noise injection is most effective for training when the noise is added to the input images.

the following questions:
How does noise injection affect the performance of CNNs?
the following three main questions: (1) How should we add noise to images in order to achieve the best performance in CNNs?
the following issues: 1. How to add noise to images for training CNNs?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best noise injection strategy for CNN architectures depends on the CNN architecture itself.
the best noise injection method is the one that provides the highest classification accuracy for the given CNN architecture, dataset, and training procedure.
the noise models with lower SSIM values are more effective than those with high SSIM values.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
noise injection is a powerful tool to improve the performance of CNNs, and that the most suitable noise model is the one that is the closest to the original data distribution.
noise injection is not a panacea for all problems and it should be used with caution, as there is a fine line that separates the benefits from the harms.
noise injection is a very effective method for data augmentation, especially for CNN architectures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given noise model, the optimal magnitude is the one that maximizes SSIM, and for the optimal magnitude, the best noise model is the one with highest SSIM.
the noise injection can be done at the end of the training phase, or at the beginning of the testing phase, without affecting the performance of CNNs.
noise injection should be performed with caution and with a clear understanding of the effects it has on the learning procedure, and the final model.
